unc.band: 16th-84th percentile of the Monte Carlo draws; central line = current estimate
sources: QPU: routing overhead of individual circuits at that depth (placement on the coupling map); classical: one typical-width network per size was searched, so the per-sentence spread of contraction cost is NOT covered
idle-subtracted to gross energy convention (median net/gross 0.47; gross, the central value, is the upper edge); run-to-run repeats on an L4 are queued and will be added

one-sided (downward only; the best path found is the upper edge): log10 FLOP lowered by U(0,1) x g, where g = -0.00 + 0.135 log10 FLOP (fit over 92 networks of the gain of the 600 s cotengra search over random-greedy-128, residual 0.78 decades): one path-quality model for all sizes
log-normal, sigma = 0.35 decades: error of the 4/8-layer interpolation measured on the real 5-layer circuits
Student-t prediction interval of the regression of log10(J per gate) on qubits over the measured 22-31 q points
bootstrap of the 27 post-selected Kingston calibration emulations (slope and intercept of ln F_eff), applied to all backends until their own calibrations land

IBM 25-30 kW (26 kW System Two refrigerator, arXiv:2304.14344; ~30 kW System One installations); IonQ 3.5-6.5 kW (5 kW +-30%, assumed); IQM 24-30 kW (typical mean, IQM Radiance spec; 30 kW peak, Mansfield et al. 2025)
IBM repetition delay 100-500 us (assumed; IBM docs example uses 500 us); IonQ gate and shot times +-20% (assumed); IQM 0.96-1.92 ms (CLOPS-derived upper value, half of it as lower, assumed)
not_covered: better classical algorithms than those tried (paths are upper bounds only within the searched optimisers)
hardware roadmaps (gate speed, power, connectivity changes)
error mitigation or error correction overheads
